name: Geometry3K
description: A large-scale benchmark consisting of 3,002 geometry problems with dense annotation in formal language. The dataset includes SAT-style problems collected from two high-school textbooks covering diverse geometric shapes and problem goals.

creator.name: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
creator.affiliation: Center for Vision, Cognition, Learning and Autonomy, UCLA; College of Computer Science and Technology, Zhejiang University; School of Intelligent Systems Engineering, Sun Yat-sen University; Beijing Institute of General Artificial Intelligence; Peking University; Tsinghua University

citeAs: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu. Inter-GPS: Interpretable Geometry Problem Solving with Formal Language and Symbolic Reasoning. arXiv:2105.04165v3 [cs.CL] 20 Jul 2021
rai:dataCollection: The data is collected from two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12 by two online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill, Geometryonline). Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collect each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data collected from two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12 by two online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill, Geometryonline).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each problem in Geometry3K is annotated with dense descriptions in formal language. Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collect each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. Each problem data is labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes. Each problem text and diagram is annotated with unified structural descriptions in formal language.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is collected from high school textbooks covering grades 6-12. Current text parser performs well with 97% accuracy, but diagram parser has room for improvement with a 17.5% gap between predicted and ground truth literals. The symbolic solver is not capable of solving complex problems with combined shapes and shaded areas in diagrams. Diagram parsing tends to fail if there are ambiguous annotations or multiple primitives in the diagram. Text parser has difficulty handling nested expressions and uncertain references.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is divided into train, validation, and test sets with the ratio of 0.7:0.1:0.2 (2,101 training data, 300 validation data, and 601 test data). The dataset is designed to assess algorithms' performance of geometry problem solving and is particularly suited for symbolic reasoning and interpretable problem solving.
